record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Is it true that, for any polynomial P with complex coefficients, the mapping f 7→ P ∗ (D)(P f ), where P ∗ (z) = P (z), is a bijection of E onto E? The proposer can prove that this is true when P is a homogeneous polynomial; and D. J. Newman told the proposer that he could prove the injectivity half of the conjecture, but the proposer has seen no details of the proof. The conjecture would follow if one could show that the partial differential equation P ∗ (D)(P f ) = z α where P ∗ (z) = P (z), has a solution f that is entire and of exponential type for every multi-index α. (H. S. Shapiro)

evidence.quote: Is it true that, for any polynomial P with complex coefficients, the mapping f 7→ P ∗ (D)(P f ), where P ∗ (z) = P (z), is a bijection of E onto E?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ denote the space of entire functions on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of exponential type (i.e., entire functions $f:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ for which there exist constants $A,B>0$ with $|f(z)|\le A e^{B\|z\|}$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$). For a polynomial $P(z)=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha z^\alpha$ with complex coefficients in $n$ variables, define the conjugate polynomial $P^*(z)=\sum_\alpha \overline{a_\alpha}\, z^\alpha$ and the constant-coefficient differential operator
$$P^*(D)=\sum_\alpha \overline{a_\alpha}\,\partial^\alpha,\qquad \partial^\alpha=\frac{\partial^{|\alpha|}}{\partial z_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots\partial z_n^{\alpha_n}}.$$
For a fixed polynomial $P$, consider the linear map
$$T_P:E\longrightarrow E,\qquad T_P(f)=P^*(D)\bigl(P\cdot f\bigr).$$
Prove or disprove: for every polynomial $P$ with complex coefficients, the map $T_P$ is a bijection of $E$ onto $E$. Equivalently, show that for every multi-index $\alpha$ the partial differential equation
$$P^*(D)\bigl(P\cdot f\bigr)=z^\alpha$$
admits an entire solution $f$ of exponential type.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions and differential operators (Fischer pairs)
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is known to hold when $P$ is homogeneous (in which case $P$ and $P^*(D)$ form a Fischer pair on entire functions). For general non-homogeneous $P$ the question has been studied as a Fischer-decomposition problem; recent work (e.g., Aldaz–Render and related papers, 2024) establishes weak/asymptotic Fischer decompositions for entire functions of sufficiently low order but does not settle the full conjecture. No complete resolution for arbitrary $P$ on $E$ appears in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved / still open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Fischer decompositions for entire functions of sufficiently low order
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers have achieved the existence of decompositions of the form f=P·q+r with P_k*(D)r=0 under certain restrictions on the order of f, and more recently proven uniqueness under certain conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on the Fischer decomposition / bijectivity problem for entire functions, not a full proof of the general conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A Fischer type decomposition theorem from the apolar inner product
status_evidence.snippet: When P is homogeneous, P and P* form a Fischer pair for entire functions. However, Shapiro conjectured that his theorem held even for non-homogeneous P and arbitrary entire functions.
status_evidence.claim: Homogeneous case is established; the non-homogeneous case is the open conjecture.
